finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only checking that it contains the substring "example.io". The substring can appear anywhere in the URL, so an attacker can reach internal or arbitrary hosts. The response body is returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF. Redirects are followed by default.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) (main.go:36), with the response streamed back via io.Copy (main.go:38)

trace.note: Only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), a substring test that does not parse the URL or check scheme or host
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, with no host or IP restrictions
Response body is copied back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The substring check is bypassable, for example http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/?example.io, http://example.io.attacker.com/, or http://attacker.com/#example.io. No URL parsing, scheme allowlist, host allowlist or private-IP blocking is applied. Redirects are followed. The /cdn handler's exact-hostname allowlist is not applied here.

verdict.guard_found: none (only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") substring check at main.go:32, which does not close the finding)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes `logo` from r.FormValue, main.go:32 only does a substring check for "example.io", and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and streams the body back at main.go:38, so there is no host or scheme validation and the SSRF is full-read.
